title: Oct 24 Results: Sometimes You Just Miss
summary: Oct 24 brought us a humbling 0-1 night. We've seen worse, but that doesn't make it sting less.

content.value:
## A Night to Forget

Look, I've been doing this long enough to know that some nights just don't go your way. October 24th was one of those nights. We had one game on the slate, felt decent about our Rays pick at 52%, and... well, Milwaukee had other plans. That's baseball, folks.

## What Happened in Milwaukee

The Rays came into American Family Field as our lean pick—nothing flashy, just a 52% probability. Basically a coin flip with the slightest edge. When you're dealing with margins that thin, you know you're playing with fire. The Brewers took care of business at home, and our model took the L.

I've seen plenty of October baseball where the home team finds that extra gear. The postseason does funny things to probabilities.

## The Reality Check

Here's the thing about a 52% pick—you're essentially saying "this could go either way, but we're leaning this direction." When it doesn't hit, you can't act surprised. The model did its job; it identified a marginal edge. Sometimes that edge doesn't materialize.

I remember the 2003 playoffs when the Marlins went on their run. They won plenty of games they had no business winning on paper. That's October for you.

content.title: 📊 The Numbers
content.sub: Our only pick didn't connect, but that's the game

content.value:
## Looking Ahead

No games scheduled for tomorrow, which gives us all a chance to reset. Sometimes a day off is exactly what you need after a rough night. The model will be ready when the next slate comes around.

In my years covering this game, I've learned that you can't let one bad night—or even one bad week—shake your foundation. You trust the process, you learn what you can, and you move forward. That's been true since the days of box scores in newspapers, and it's still true now.

We'll be back when the games return. Until then, enjoy the breather.

author: Max
